concepts.title: Stack Size after Pushes and Pops
concepts.definition: A stack is a linear data structure that admits inserts and deletes at one end, the TOP, so it obeys LIFO: PUSH adds at the top, POP removes from the top, and the element stored last leaves first.
concepts.key_idea: Popping the glass numbered 2 from the pile of Figure 3.2 exposes the glass beneath it, never a middle one.
question_patterns: Starting from an empty stack, 4 pushes are followed by 2 pops. How many elements remain?
A stack holds 3 elements; two pushes and one pop happen next. What is its size afterwards?
State TRUE or FALSE: PUSH may result in underflow and stack does not follow LIFO.
Which single end of a stack do PUSH and POP use, and what is that end called?
In the glass-stack demonstration, which glass leaves first and why?

solution_steps.explain: Each push adds one and each pop removes one.
Add the net change to the starting size.

worked_examples.q: A stack starts with 3 elements. After two PUSH operations and one POP, how many elements does it hold?

concepts.title: Applications of the Stack in Practice
concepts.definition: Everywhere the most recent item must be served first, a stack fits: reversing a string, undo and redo in editors, the BACK button of a browser replaying page history, and checking that parentheses in an expression nest correctly.
concepts.formula: most recent change -> undone or redone first
concepts.key_idea: Browser history keeps visited pages as a stack, so two BACK clicks from page P3 land on page P1.
question_patterns: Why is a stack the right structure for the undo feature of an editor?
From page P3, how do two clicks of the BACK button reach page P1, and which structure stores the history?
Name two real-life situations that behave like a stack.
How does a stack help in reversing a string?
Why does a compiler use a stack while checking matched parentheses?

solution_steps.explain: Whenever the required order is last-in-first-out, a stack models the situation; otherwise a queue or another structure fits better.

concepts.title: Infix, Prefix and Postfix Notations
concepts.definition: One expression has three written forms: infix places operators between operands as x * y + z, prefix (Polish) places them before the operands, and postfix (reverse Polish) places them after, which removes the need for parentheses and precedence rules.
concepts.key_idea: Prefix and postfix expressions evaluate in one left-to-right traversal because operator order is already fixed.
question_patterns: Write the postfix and prefix forms of the infix expression (x + y)/(z * 5).
Why do postfix expressions need no parentheses at all?
State TRUE or FALSE: in postfix notation operators come after operands.
Who introduced the polish notation, and what distinguishes it from reverse polish notation?
Convert 3 * (4 + 5) into both prefix and postfix forms.

solution_steps.explain: Keep the evaluation order of BODMAS, then move each operator just before (prefix) or just after (postfix) its two operands, dropping the parentheses.

worked_examples.q: Which notation places operators before their operands?

concepts.title: Evaluating a Postfix Expression
concepts.definition: A postfix expression evaluates with a stack: operands are pushed, and each operator pops two values, applies itself and pushes the result back, so the final single stack entry is the answer, as in 7 8 2 * 4 / + giving 11.
concepts.key_idea: Only operands are pushed during evaluation; each operator consumes exactly the top two stack values.
question_patterns: Evaluate the postfix expression 7 8 2 * 4 / + showing the stack after each step.
What does the stack contain just before the final plus operator of 7 8 2 * 4 / + is applied?
Why does a postfix evaluation need only one left-to-right scan?
What does Algorithm 3.2 report if the stack does not end with a single element?
Trace the pushes and pops for the expression 5 6 2 + * 12 4 / - .

solution_steps.explain: The operator * pops 8 and 2 and pushes their product 16.
The operator / pops 16 and 4 and pushes the quotient.
The final + pops 4 and 7, leaving the single result.

concepts.title: Postfix Evaluation with Letter Operands
concepts.definition: When postfix operands are letters, substitute the given values first and then run the same push-pop evaluation, for example A B + C * with A=3, B=5, C=1 becomes (3 + 5) * 1 which is 8.
concepts.key_idea: Substitute the letter values before evaluation so only numbers ride on the stack.
question_patterns: Evaluate A B + C * for A=3, B=5, C=1, showing the stack after each operation.
Evaluate A B * C / D * for A=3, B=5, C=1, D=4.
Why must the values of A, B, C and D be known before a postfix expression of letters is evaluated?
Which pair of operands does the first operator of A B * C / D * consume?
Convert A + B - C * D into postfix and then evaluate it for A=3, B=5, C=1, D=4.

solution_steps.explain: The + operator pops B and A and pushes their sum.
The * operator pops the sum and C, pushing the product.

worked_examples.q: With A=3, B=5 and C=1, what does the postfix expression A B + C * evaluate to?

concepts.title: Converting Infix to Postfix
concepts.definition: Algorithm 3.1 converts infix to postfix using a stack for operators: operands append straight to the output string, left parentheses wait on the stack, operators pop higher-precedence elders first, and a right parenthesis pops until its matching left one, discarding the pair.
concepts.key_idea: Only operators and parentheses ever ride on the stack during conversion; operands go directly to the output.
question_patterns: Convert the infix expression A + B - C * D into postfix, showing the stack and string at each step.
Convert A * ((C + D)/E) into postfix notation.
Show the conversion of (x + y)/(z * 8) into postfix expression.
During conversion, why does a right parenthesis pop operators until the left parenthesis appears?
Which items are pushed on the stack while converting an infix expression to postfix?

solution_steps.explain: Append operands to the output, park operators on the stack by precedence, empty the stack at closing parentheses, and flush the stack at the end of input.

worked_examples.q: During infix to postfix conversion, which items go straight to the output string?

concepts.title: Matching Parentheses with a Stack
concepts.definition: A compiler validates nesting by pushing every opening parenthesis and popping on every closing one; the expression is balanced only if each closing parenthesis finds its partner on the stack top and the stack ends empty.
concepts.formula: balanced -> every ')' pops a '(' and final stack is empty
concepts.key_idea: For ((2+3)*(4/2))+2 the two left parentheses are popped in reverse order, proving correct nesting.
question_patterns: Show step by step how a stack matches the parentheses of ((2+3)*(4/2))+2.
What stack condition signals mismatched parentheses in an expression?
Why must the stack be empty at the end of a balanced expression?
Trace the push and pop actions for the expression (x + y)/(z * 8).
Which exception-like condition arises when a closing parenthesis arrives with an empty stack?

solution_steps.explain: Push on '(' and pop on ')'; a pop from an empty stack or a non-empty final stack both declare the expression unbalanced.

worked_examples.q: In the expression ((2+3)*(4/2))+2, how many opening parentheses get pushed?

concepts.title: Stack Implementation Using a List
concepts.definition: Python builds a stack on a list whose right end is the TOP: append() plays PUSH, pop() plays POP, len() gives the size, and a helper checks emptiness so a pop from an empty stack reports underflow instead of crashing.
concepts.key_idea: Because append and pop act on the rightmost end, no explicit TOP variable is needed.
concepts.textbook_ref: lecs103.txt, section 3.4, functions isEmpty, opPush, opPop, size, top, display
question_patterns: Give the output of the code where numberList = [10, 20, 30], 40 is appended, and pop() runs twice into result.
Which built-in list methods implement PUSH and POP in Python?
What does the isEmpty function return for an empty stack, and why is it checked before popping?
Why is no overflow possible for the list-based stack of section 3.4?
Write the function top that returns the most recent element without deleting it.
What message does opPrint show when a pop is attempted on an empty stack?

solution_steps.action: map stack words to list calls
solution_steps.explain: PUSH becomes append at the right end, POP becomes pop from the same end, and the emptiness test guards against underflow.

worked_examples.q: Which list method plays the role of PUSH on a Python-list stack?

worked_examples.title: Stack trace of 7 8 2 * 4 / +
worked_examples.problem: Evaluate the postfix expression 7 8 2 * 4 / + exactly as Algorithm 3.2 does, stating the stack after each operation.

steps.explain: Pop 4 and 7, push the sum 11, which is the lone survivor.

worked_examples.answer_note: The stack grows 7, 8, 2; collapses to 7, 16 then 7, 4; and ends with the single result 11.

worked_examples.title: Evaluating A B + C * with values
worked_examples.problem: For A = 3, B = 5 and C = 1, evaluate the postfix expression A B + C * with stack statuses.
worked_examples.answer_note: The expression evaluates to 8, with the stack holding 3, 5 then 8 then empty.
